summary: [Client Manager][BE FE QA] New Client Manager (Finance View) / Splitted to Tasks

ai.s: A dedicated Finance view in the new Client Manager lets Finance review, approve and reject customer environments inside the platform, with a full audit trail.
ai.pr: Finance approved or rejected new customer environments entirely outside the system through async communication, with no central interface and no recorded audit trail.
ai.wy: Second step of the Onboarding Journey after TAM environment creation; bringing Finance approval in-house centralises control.
ai.oc: A Finance role and a "Customer Management" screen with Kanban and list views, status tabs and a review side panel with an approval checklist to approve or reject environments.

ai.s: A guided onboarding flow takes new organisers through account, event and billing setup and recommends modules suited to their event.
ai.pr: New organisers had no structured path from signup to a configured event, so setup was high-friction and the information needed for personalisation and billing was not collected.
ai.wy: Part of the Onboarding Journey: reduce setup friction and drive activation and module adoption after signup.
ai.oc: A five-step onboarding flow (About You, Event Setup, Billing, Tell Us About Your Event, Unlock More Value) with skip, dashboard landing, decision-table module recommendations and stored responses.

ai.s: An event onboarding dashboard gives TAMs and organisers one place to see setup progress per module, manage team members and resume onboarding.
ai.pr: Understanding event setup status meant navigating across multiple screens, with no single view of progress, team members or what still needed attention.
ai.wy: Part of the Onboarding Journey: a single source of truth for TAMs and organisers during event setup.
ai.oc: A shared dashboard with event overview cards, team member invitations, module-level and overall completion percentages, module navigation and a continue-onboarding entry point.

ai.s: Automatic onboarding emails keep TAMs, Finance and organisers informed when environments and events are created, approved, rejected or go live.
ai.pr: There were no system notifications for key onboarding lifecycle changes, so TAMs, Finance and organisers relied on manual communication to learn about approvals, rejections and status changes.
ai.wy: Part of the Onboarding Journey: keep every role informed of lifecycle actions taken in the Admin Panel.
ai.oc: Triggered emails for TAMs (assignment, client/event approved or rejected), Finance (new client, re-send, test to live, dates changed) and organisers (onboarding, test to live).

ai.s: The Visitor team defined availability and latency SLOs for the endpoints it owns, giving measurable reliability targets for its part of the platform.
ai.pr: Endpoints owned by the Visitor team had no documented, measurable reliability targets, so service-level health was not visible.
ai.wy: Engineering-wide initiative for each team to establish SLOs and gain full visibility of platform health at service level.
ai.oc: An inventory of Visitor team endpoints with availability and latency SLOs, based on Grafana data and documented in Confluence using the SLO template.
